doc.title: Michael Max Fleming interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

title: Pay for black and white musicians around Cincinnati
summary: He earned $10 a night, against $15 across the river where casinos paid better, and he reflects on why smart employers pay well.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Do you recall what you made on that gig?
Oh man you ask some nasty questions.
Do you want to know what color underwear I have on? Tough questions. Okay I’ll tell you. Oh man, if I had known [inaudible] agree to do this interview here. Wow you’re good. Okay.
I made four dollars on my first gig.
But you’re shameless. You don’t ask, you don’t care what I think of you. But anyway here we go. I’m going to answer you.

At the time all the other musicians in Cincinnati, black musicians, because black musicians did one thing and the white musicians — we’re talking about the 50s. We’re not talking about, well there’s some strange stuff going on now but we’re not talking about that. They made ten dollars a night. Across the river you made fifteen.
Was that because of the white community on one side of the river and the black community on the other?

No, no, no. With the river it had to do with the nature of — they had casinos. They had money and they were smart people. Smart people. I’m not a businessman — oh I get myself in so much — but smart people know that sometimes if you pay people better they’ll, they’ll appreciate the job better and not think about going somewhere else. Or © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

there’s a lot of reasons why you pay people that short-sighted people don’t understand it. But there’s people, “Well but I’m losing money.” Yeah but you’ve got to look at the big picture. Smart people pay people and they get better results. That’s just what I know. I’m not a businessman. I’m not an economics professor. I’m just a plain old jazz musician that’s been all over the world. That’s all.
